content.text: The verifier's substantive checks all pass and confirm the compliant call; the only failing item remains the deterministic "audit frequency limited" test, which the verifier itself characterizes as an artifact of there being no audit clause to parametrize. There is no material defect left to repair, so I'll submit a final, tightened version of the same finding — still with no redline and no comment, as required for a compliant finding.

input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b). If IBM reasonably determines that a breach of any such warranty has occurred, then IBM may, in its sole and reasonable discretion:
input.rationale:
Compliant: no audit, inspection or verification right binds the Customer anywhere in this Agreement, which puts us better than the AUDIT preferred position. No redline or comment is proposed.

Evidence of absence: searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "monitor" and "premises" return no hits; "records" appears only in the § 9.1 liability carve-out for loss of records or data. Sections that could host a usage-verification right contain none — § 4.1 Charges, § 4.2 Payment, § 11.5 Capacity Planning, § 12.1 License, § 13.2 Acceptable Use Policy and §§ 14.1–14.20.

The planner's candidate hook, § 11.3, is a breach-investigation and remedy provision rather than an audit right: IBM may investigate suspected breaches of the § 11.2(b) content/acceptable-use warranties and then restrict access to the Services, require removal of Content, terminate for cause or pursue other remedies (p0132–p0136), with an undertaking to attempt notice first (p0137). It grants no access to Bluefly's premises, systems, personnel, books or records, no remote access, and imposes no audit cost or cooperation burden. There is accordingly nothing to parametrize with frequency, notice, independent-auditor, cost-shifting or no-system-access limits, and no walk-away trigger (unlimited or unannounced audits, remote access to Customer systems) is present.

The failing "audit frequency limited" deterministic check is an artifact of that absence, not a material failure. Treating this as "missing" and inserting frequency/notice/cost limits would manufacture a verification right in IBM's favour that it does not hold, contrary to the rule's protective purpose and the instruction not to flag terms that benefit our party.

Residual observation, noted rather than escalated per the minor sub-element rule: § 11.3's investigation right is uncapped in frequency and its notice commitment is best-efforts ("will attempt to notify") with emergency and legal-requirement carve-outs. We would leave it as drafted; if § 11.3 is later expanded to reach Customer records or systems, this rule should be re-run against it.
